title: Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense Message Volume
exclusions: Counts message-log events. Audit and connection logs use the same sourcetype and the add-on publishes no field that separates them, so this input must be set to Message Logs only.

controlTest.positiveScenario: With the input set to Message Logs, send a test message through Email Threat Defense. The next hour's count increases.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Clear the Message Logs selection. The user guide then uses a different API path or stops message events, and the next hour falls to zero.

dataSources: `index=cisco_etd sourcetype=cisco:etd` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Email Threat Defense input. The user guide says log types are Connection, Audit, and Message. With none selected the input calls `POST https://api.{region}.etd.cisco.com/v1/messages/search`. With log types selected it calls `POST /v1/downloadLinks`. No field list is published, and nothing in the guide names a field that distinguishes the three log types, so this search counts events and the input is restricted to Message Logs.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Secure Email Threat Defense input.
spl:
index=cisco_etd sourcetype="cisco:etd" earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count as messages
description: Counts Cisco Secure Email Threat Defense message events per hour. The add-on writes message, audit, and connection logs as the single sourcetype cisco:etd and publishes no field that tells them apart, so the input for this search is set to Message Logs only.
value: Phishing and business-email-compromise verdicts only help if the analysed messages are arriving in Splunk. This count is the check that the message log, which carries those verdicts, is still being collected.
implementation: Create the Email Threat Defense input with API key, client id, secret, and region. Select Message Logs only. Chart cisco:etd events per hour.
visualization: Column chart of messages per hour over 24 hours.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Weekends** — mail volume drops. Compare with the same hour last week.

2. **Mixed log types** — if Audit Logs are also selected, the count mixes administrator actions with messages. Keep this input on Message Logs.

**Suppression:** alert when a business hour is zero.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• An Email Threat Defense API key, client id, client secret, and region (the host is api.{region}.etd.cisco.com).
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_etd`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Secure Email Threat Defense card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_etd`.
• The input writes `cisco:etd`.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=cisco_etd sourcetype="cisco:etd" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_etd sourcetype="cisco:etd" earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count as messages
```

Understanding this SPL
• The user guide's log-type control decides which API is called. Restrict this input to Message Logs so the count is messages.
• No verdict field is documented, so the panel does not filter phishing versus spam.

Step 3 — Validate
• In Email Threat Defense, open the message search for the same hour. Messages there and a zero panel means the API client or region is wrong.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Email Threat Defense and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• HTTP 401: the API key, client id, or secret does not match the region.
• Counts that include administrator actions: Audit Logs is selected on this input. Clear it. Audit events are not given their own sourcetype.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We count the email messages Cisco's threat defense analyses each hour, so we know phishing verdicts are still arriving.
